digest:
## 🔬 Major Technical Developments

### VideoLAN Publishes Dav2d For Open-Source AV2 Decoder
URL: https://code.videolan.org/videolan/dav2d
VideoLAN ships first open-source AV2 decoder, following dav1d playbook that became industry standard
The team behind dav1d—which Apple, Google, and Netflix all adopted for AV1—is now tackling Alliance for Open Media's next-gen codec. AV2 promises 30%+ compression gains over AV1, critical for 8K streaming and bandwidth-constrained mobile. If dav2d matches dav1d's performance dominance, it becomes the de facto decoder for the next decade of video infrastructure.

### A physics engine with incremental rollback for multiplayer games
URL: https://easel.games/blog/2026-rollback-physics
New physics engine solves netcode holy grail: deterministic rollback without full state rewrites
Incremental rollback means games can correct mispredictions by replaying only affected objects, not entire world state. This addresses the core technical barrier keeping physics-heavy multiplayer games locked to client-server models. Potential to unlock new genres of competitive physics games that previously couldn't handle latency gracefully.

### Unsigned sizes: a five year mistake
URL: https://c3-lang.org/blog/unsigned-sizes-a-five-year-mistake/
C3 language reverses unsigned size decision after five years of real-world friction
Practical post-mortem on a systems language design choice. The takeaway: even in performance-critical contexts, signed sizes prevent more bugs than unsigned sizes catch. Relevant signal for anyone evaluating Rust, Zig, or C3 for infrastructure work.

## 💼 Business & Market Signals

### AI-generated actors and scripts are now ineligible for Oscars
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/02/ai-generated-actors-and-scripts-are-now-ineligible-for-oscars/
Academy draws hard line: AI-generated content cannot compete for film's top honors
This creates a two-tier content market—Oscar-eligible human-made vs. AI-assisted productions. Studios now face explicit tradeoffs between AI cost savings and awards prestige. Watch for similar rules from Cannes, BAFTA, and guilds; this fragments the addressable market for AI-generated entertainment tools.

### Uber wants to turn its millions of drivers into a sensor grid for self-driving companies
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/01/uber-wants-to-turn-its-millions-of-drivers-into-a-sensor-grid-for-self-driving-companies/
Uber monetizes its driver fleet as mobile mapping infrastructure for AV competitors
Uber is building AV Labs into a data-as-a-service business, turning the same drivers robotaxis will eventually replace into the training pipeline for those robotaxis. With millions of daily trips, Uber could offer fresher, denser mapping data than Waymo or Cruise collect internally. This is Uber hedging its autonomous future while extracting near-term revenue from its largest cost center.

### Farewell, Jeeves: Ask.com shuts down
URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/02/farewell-jeeves-ask-com-shuts-down/
IAC kills Ask.com—legacy search finally loses to AI-native alternatives
The last major pre-Google search survivor exits. IAC's decision signals that maintaining traditional search infrastructure no longer pencils against ChatGPT, Perplexity, and integrated AI assistants. Any remaining search arbitrage plays are now in niche verticals, not general web.

## 📋 Case Studies & Deep Dives

### Six Years Perfecting Maps on WatchOS
URL: https://www.david-smith.org/blog/2026/04/29/maps-on-watchos/
Indie developer documents six-year iteration cycle building maps for Apple Watch constraints
Deep technical narrative on building for extreme resource constraints: 44mm screen, limited touch, offline-first requirements. Useful pattern library for anyone shipping on constrained devices—from wearables to embedded displays. The longevity itself is notable: sustained indie development on a single feature vertical.

### The agent harness belongs outside the sandbox
URL: https://www.mendral.com/blog/agent-harness-belongs-outside-sandbox
Architecture proposal separates AI agent control plane from execution environment
Argues agent orchestration should run privileged while sandboxing only execution—inverting current patterns where everything runs in a single container. This matters as AI agents gain system access; getting the security boundary wrong means either capability limitations or exploitable surfaces.

### NHS Goes To War Against Open Source
URL: https://shkspr.mobi/blog/2026/05/nhs-goes-to-war-against-open-source/
UK health system tightens procurement rules in ways that effectively exclude open-source vendors
Security-motivated policy changes are blocking open-source solutions from NHS contracts. The pattern—using compliance requirements to preference incumbent vendors—is replicable across government procurement globally. Open-source enterprise vendors (Red Hat, Canonical, SUSE) face growing public sector headwinds despite cost and flexibility advantages.

## ⚡ Signal vs. Noise

The through-line today is platform leverage shifting. Uber is repositioning drivers as infrastructure rather than labor. The Academy is using eligibility rules to define what counts as "film." NHS procurement is using security theater to lock in vendors. The technical work—better codecs, smarter physics engines, cleaner language design—continues underneath, but the distribution and monetization battles are increasingly fought through rule-setting rather than product superiority. Watch for more incumbents discovering that governance is a moat.
